This is one example of an ease curve, or a curve that takes values between 0 and 1 and smooths out the result (if we just used the function f(x) = x instead, the perlin noise would look more like pyramids than hills and valleys).

For this tutorial, I go left to right, row by row, meaning that (1,0) is one item after (0,0) whereas (0,1) is a full row of items after (0,0).
If needed though, you can adapt it to work with columns instead.

I can't stress enough how useful or important vectors can be...

If you don't know what vectors are or are still unsure about them, I highly recommend looking at the tutorial I shared in the project description to help with understanding this part.

Based on the coordinate (x,y), we get four vectors pointing from the corners of the grid square it's in to the coordinate and get the dot products of those vectors with the 2D list vectors at those corners. 

Then, we run the x coordinate relative to the grid square it's in into the ease curve function and use that result to interpolate between the left and right corner dot products. We do the same again with the y coordinate relative to the grid square and interpolate between the interpolated top and bottom results.

That last part is basically a fancy way of saying that we average the dot products at the four corners in such a way that the result is smooth and looks nice.
